summary: A value written as '${esc(x)}' inside a data-on-* attribute was not safe: the browser decodes the entity before oo-on.js parses the attribute, so an apostrophe closes the grammar's string and the rest runs as further allowed calls (reproduced in Chromium with the real parser). 28 values in 21 attributes now use ${esc(JSON.stringify(x))}; tests/test_oo_on_argument_ratchet.py forbids the old form and lists 22 raw single-quoted pairs the code itself chooses, each with its reason; a Node test replays 20 hostile values through the real parser (the old form is kept as a control that injects). Reachability with an apostrophe was NOT traced for any of the 28. Not browser-verified.
